summary: Backend-only testing for RideReserve v3 features: Verified Driver Badge, Cancel Booking, and aggregation-based /vehicles/search. Added /app/backend/tests/test_v3_features.py with 17 tests (3 badge, 4 cancel, 3 search-aggregation, 7 regression). Full suite (all 3 test files): 54/54 passed in 9.43s. Verified: (1) driver_verified flips to true only after 5+ five-star reviews aggregated across ALL of the driver's vehicles; flag propagates on BOTH /api/vehicles/{id} and /api/vehicles/search; reviews on other drivers do NOT verify; 4-star reviews do NOT count toward the counter (five_star_count stays 0). (2) POST /api/bookings/{id}/cancel: owner-only (returns 404 for stranger), sets status='cancelled', releases seats verified by /vehicles/{id}/seats booked_seats no longer contains cancelled seats, refunds driver wallet by exact driver_earning amount, records a 'debit' transaction linked to booking_id, unpaid cancel does NOT create a debit txn, idempotent (2nd cancel returns 200 + status='cancelled' + does NOT create a duplicate debit). (3) /api/vehicles/search aggregation returns seats_available correctly = total_seats - booked seats for that travel_date; unrelated dates show full availability; latency well under 2s over public URL (typically <200ms). (4) Regression pass: OTP auth, seat 409 conflict, 50/50 commission split (driver gets exactly 225 on 450 fare), review creation, referral apply, admin approvals, /config, /geocode all green.
action_items: No blockers. All 3 new features work as specified.

Optional: on cancel of a paid booking, consider also refunding the platform commission (currently only driver_earning is reversed via debit txn; platform commission remains in the 'commission' txn stream). Not in spec, but audit-cleaner.

Optional: expose a passenger-side refund transaction (currently the passenger's paid_at flag on booking is retained; no explicit passenger 'refunded' txn). Spec only requires driver-side negative txn, which is present.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:789 _recompute_driver_verification writes driver_verified + driver_five_star_count on ALL of the driver's vehicles (approved+pending). Good - ensures /vehicles/search and /vehicles/{id} both return the flag consistently.
server.py:673 cancel endpoint auth check is '(not b or b.passenger_id != user.user_id)' returning 404 for both non-existent and non-owner. Consistent with request spec ('404 for others').
server.py:678 idempotent early-return when status=='cancelled' — verified via test_cancel_idempotent (no duplicate debit).
server.py:403 /vehicles/search uses a SINGLE aggregation pipeline over bookings (unwind + group) — proper N+1 fix.
server.py:611 /bookings/mine batches vehicle lookups with $in ({vehicle_id: {$in: vids}}) — also fixed.
server.py is now ~1063 lines; still worth splitting into routers as previously flagged.

Minor: cancel of a PAID booking does not reverse the referral bonus if the cancelled booking was the referee's first paid ride — a passenger could cancel and re-book to abuse the flow. Not in current scope but worth tracking.
seed_data_creation: None persistent. Tests create fresh phone-OTP users (prefix +9197...) and fresh vehicles with plate prefixes 'TS*', 'CNCL*', 'RGA*'. Uses seeded vehicles veh_demo_car_01/tempo_01/bus_01 and driver user_demo_driver.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 3 v3 features are backend-verified. driver_verified flag lives on BOTH the vehicle doc (via update_many) and the user doc (drivers). Threshold = 5 five-star reviews across all of driver's vehicles. Cancel endpoint is idempotent and reverses only driver_earning (not platform commission). /vehicles/search now uses aggregation; response shape unchanged for callers (adds seats_available). Frontend derives Trip Reminders banner locally from /bookings/mine — no backend endpoint added for that (verified spec-consistent). Public API: https://mobility-reserve-3.preview.emergentagent.com/api. Mongo: mongodb://localhost:27017/ride_reserve_db.
